newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Total sees improved profitability.
newsitem.headline: French Total sees improved profitability.

text.p: French energy company Total said on Wednesday that it expected its profitability to improve in the next few years.

"Return on equity rose to 10.3 percent in 1996. This level of profitability is on line with targets set by the group to increase return on equity to 10 percent in 1998 and 12 percent in 2000 assuming a less favourable reference environment based on the 1994/1995 period," Total said in a statement announcing its 1996 earnings.
"Continuing production growth and ongoing productivity gains projected over the next few years should allow the company to improve profitability relative to the 1996 level of return on Equity."
Total said its net income in 1996 rose to 5.6 billion francs ($1 billion) from 2.2 billion francs in 1995.
It said its net debt to equity ratio was 19 percent as of December 31, 1996, comapred to 18 percent at year end 1995.
"Capital expenditures were 16 billion francs in 1996," Total said.
"Capital expenditures are projected to increase to 18 billion frances with 61 percent allocated to the upstream sector."
